scenes.text: The most famous speech in American history lasted about two minutes.
On November nineteenth, eighteen sixty three, Abraham Lincoln spoke at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania.
Crowds came to dedicate a cemetery for soldiers killed in the battle there.
But Lincoln wasn't even the main speaker.
That honor went to Edward Everett, who talked for about two hours.
His speech was around thirteen thousand words long.
Then Lincoln stood up and said just two hundred seventy two words.
He finished so fast that photographers barely had time to get a clean shot.
Contrary to myth, he didn't scribble it on an envelope on the train.
But the day after the ceremony, Everett wrote Lincoln a letter.
He said he wished he had come as near to the central idea in two hours as Lincoln did in two minutes.
Lincoln himself had said the world would little note what was said there.
Today, five handwritten copies survive, and the words are carved in stone at the Lincoln Memorial.
What short speech or quote has stuck with you the most?

title: The greatest speech in US history lasted 2 minutes 🎤
caption: On Nov 19, 1863, Edward Everett spoke for about 2 hours at Gettysburg. Lincoln followed with just 272 words, and that's the one everyone remembers.
